messages:
oncall-bot: [pager] SEV2 - dedicated-pool-12 high tail latency detected. p99 > 5s, autoscaler not progressing. Auto-triggered from latency rule.

oncall-bot: Alerts summary: p95 1.1s -> 2.4s, p99 5.9s -> 8.2s; queue_depth (route:/v1/generate) 120 -> 920; streaming stall count spike +280%

tj: I'm on the page. joining. @maya @erica please confirm customer impact and whether this is isolated to pool-12.

maya: Confirmed glyph and beta-suite tenants seeing timeouts and stream stalls. Reproduced with long-gen (~1.2k tokens) - stream stalls around 6-8s before chunk arrives.

erica: Autoscaler events show a scale attempt at 17:22:30 UTC but nodes stuck in warmup state `loading-model`. kubernetes shows 3 pods Pending/ContainerCreating for >2m. Kernel logs show repeated mmap failures on gpu-33.

sam: `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pools` output (snippet):
```
NAME                     READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
worker-4-7f9d8           0/1     CrashLoopBackOff    3          5m
gpu-33-provision         0/1     ContainerCreating   0          3m
worker-6-9c2a1           1/1     Running             0          10m
```

lead-sre: Handoff - I'm taking incident lead. Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce bundling/continuous batching on heavy route 2) fail traffic to hosted fallback for affected tenants 3) trigger manual capacity add and keep autoscaler paused until warm nodes stable.

maya: Runbook step: disable batching on route -> `redwoodctl route update /v1/generate --batching=off` (note: will raise per-token cost). Executed at 1845678950.

erica: Applying routing policy to send traffic to hosted fallback: `routing set /v1/generate tenant=glyph fallback=hosted:gpt-medium`

ops-bot: Manual scale request received: `infra scale-pool dedicated-pool-12 --delta=+3` by tj at 1845678952. Provisioning started, estimated time ~200s.

maya: Observing metrics: queue_depth falling 920 -> 410 after disabling batching and routing fallback. p99 dropping from 8.2s -> 3.1s but streaming stalls still visible for long requests.

sam: Collected logs from worker-4 before crash:
```
[2028-08-15T17:22:14Z] kernel: mmap failed: -12
[2028-08-15T17:22:15Z] worker-4: eviction: KV cache pressure high
[2028-08-15T17:22:16Z] runtime: model load timeout after 125s
```

lead-sre: Temporary mitigations reduced user-visible p99 to ~2.5-3.2s overall. Streaming stalls persist for sequences >800 tokens; likely KV-cache cold misses and chunked I/O contention during warmup. Next steps: collect diagnostic tarball from stuck nodes, restart ones with mmap errors after collecting dmesg, and consider enabling quantized model variant for heavy tenants to reduce load.

maya: Notifying CS: "We're mitigating elevated latency and intermittent streaming stalls for long-generation requests impacting a subset of traffic. We've applied fallbacks and added capacity; working on root cause. We'll follow up with timeline and postmortem."

cs-rep: Customer (glyph) reported: "We saw ~10-12% request failures and slow responses between 17:20-17:36 UTC. Appreciate the quick fallback — please keep us posted."

tj: I've triggered node diagnostics collection: `infra collect-diagnostics --node gpu-33 --out /tmp/diag-gpu-33-1845678958.tar.gz`. Also performed manual scale-up confirmation at 1845678990 (pool count now 6).

erica: Diagnostics show repeated user-space OOMs tied to worker process memory spikes during model mmap; kernel logs show intermittent -12 (ENOMEM) from the driver. Suspect noisy neighbor VM / host memory pressure during parallel model loads.

lead-sre: Action plan for 2-hour window: 1) complete node restarts and verify stable warmup 2) re-enable autoscaler with throttled step-policy (max +1 per 60s) 3) introduce strict token cap for fallback tenants (max_tokens=1024) 4) run canary traffic for 15m then re-open batching if stable.

maya: Scheduling post-incident review tomorrow 09:00 PT. Markers to include: p95 breach window 17:19-17:36 UTC, p99 peak 17:23 UTC, affected tenants: glyph, beta-suite, ~10% of requests impacted.

lead-sre: Recording trace id for detailed investigation: trace-id=0x7f3b2c9a. attaching logs and diag tarball to INC-184567 (internal ticket).

ops-bot: Scale completed; 3 new instances provisioned and nodes reported Ready at 1845679070.

maya: After restarts, warmup successes increased, model load latency dropped ~80% for subsequent loads. Queue depth now steady ~45. No further 5xx spikes in the last 5m.

oncall-bot: Incident status updated to MITIGATED by lead-sre at 1845679180.

tj: We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then transition to monitoring-only. Please add any follow-ups to INC-184567 and include any customer communication drafts. Thanks everyone for quick response :clap:
